# Memory map

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_memmap.py from scripts/memmap.yaml. Do not edit. -->

All addresses are byte addresses on the 32-bit core bus. Every number in this file comes from `scripts/memmap.yaml`. An access to an address that is not listed below gets an error response, which the core reports as an access fault (docs/SPEC.md §6.3).

## Memory configurations

- **GDS**: 2 x sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 (1 KB IMEM + 1 KB DMEM); used for the layout
- **SIM**: behavioural memories with the same 1rw1r interface, 32 KB each; used for CoreMark and arch tests

## Regions

| Region | Base | Size (GDS) | Size (SIM) | Ports | Access | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BOOTROM | `0x00000000` | 256 B | 256 B | I, D | RX | CORE | Boot ROM (synthesised logic). Reset vector. Holds the boot loader (SPEC §7). |
| IMEM | `0x10000000` | 1024 B | 32768 B | I, D | RWX | MEM | Instruction memory. Fetch uses SRAM port 1 (read-only); data loads/stores use port 0. |
| DMEM | `0x20000000` | 1024 B | 32768 B | D | RW | MEM | Data memory (data, stack). Not executable (fetch gives an instruction access fault). |
| APB | `0x40000000` | 65536 B | 65536 B | D | RW | mixed | Peripheral window, 16 slots of 4 KB, through the bus-to-APB bridge. Word accesses only. |

## APB peripherals

Each peripheral has one 4 KB slot. Accesses must be 32-bit and word-aligned. Access types:

- **RO**: read-only; a write gets an error response and changes nothing.
- **RW**: read/write.
- **W1C**: write 1 to clear.
- **WO**: write-only; reads return 0.

Unlisted bits read 0, and writes to them are ignored.

| Base | Peripheral | Domain | IRQC source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x40000000` | [UART](#uart) | PERI | 0 | 16550-lite UART (feature set of a 16550 - programmable divisor, 8N1, 16-byte FIFOs, interrupts - with a simpler register layout; not register-compatible). |
| `0x40001000` | [GPIO](#gpio) | PERI | 1 | 8-bit GPIO with a direction register and per-pin edge interrupts. |
| `0x40002000` | [TIMER](#timer) | AON | — | CLINT-style machine timer and software interrupt (privileged spec §3.2.1 and §3.1.9). |
| `0x40003000` | [IRQC](#irqc) | CORE | — | Simple 8-source interrupt controller. |
| `0x40004000` | [SYSCTRL](#sysctrl) | AON | — | Boot and wake reason, scratch, boot strap (AON, survives DEEP_SLEEP). |
| `0x40005000` | [PMU](#pmu) | AON | 2 | P2 power-management unit (soc-pmu-sequencer / multipower). |

## UART

16550-lite UART (feature set of a 16550 - programmable divisor, 8N1, 16-byte FIFOs, interrupts - with a simpler register layout; not register-compatible). The RX start-bit wake detector is a separate AON block (SPEC §8.4).

| Address | Register | Access | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x40000000` | UART_DATA | RW | `0x00000000` | Write pushes a byte into the TX FIFO (dropped if full, sets IRQ_STATUS.TX_OVF). |
| `0x40000004` | UART_STATUS | RO | `0x00000005` | FIFO and line status. |
| `0x40000008` | UART_CTRL | RW | `0x00000000` | Enables and FIFO flush. |
| `0x4000000c` | UART_BAUD_DIV | RW | `0x000001b1` | Bit period in clock cycles minus 1, for TX and RX. |
| `0x40000010` | UART_IRQ_EN | RW | `0x00000000` | Interrupt enables, same bit layout as IRQ_STATUS. |
| `0x40000014` | UART_IRQ_STATUS | W1C | `0x00000002` | RX and TX are levels (not clearable); error bits are sticky, write 1 to clear. |

| Register | Bits | Field | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DATA | [7:0] | DATA | `0x0` | Byte. |
| STATUS | [20:16] | RX_LEVEL | `0x0` | Bytes in the RX FIFO (0-16). |
| STATUS | [12:8] | TX_LEVEL | `0x0` | Bytes in the TX FIFO (0-16). |
| STATUS | [3] | RX_FULL | `0x0` | RX FIFO holds 16 bytes. |
| STATUS | [2] | RX_EMPTY | `0x1` | RX FIFO empty. |
| STATUS | [1] | TX_FULL | `0x0` | TX FIFO holds 16 bytes. |
| STATUS | [0] | TX_EMPTY | `0x1` | TX FIFO empty and shifter idle. |
| CTRL | [11:8] | RX_THRESH | `0x0` | RX interrupt when RX_LEVEL > RX_THRESH. |
| CTRL | [3] | RX_FLUSH | `0x0` | Write 1 to empty the RX FIFO (reads 0). |
| CTRL | [2] | TX_FLUSH | `0x0` | Write 1 to empty the TX FIFO (reads 0). |
| CTRL | [1] | RX_EN | `0x0` | Receiver enabled. |
| CTRL | [0] | TX_EN | `0x0` | Transmitter enabled. |
| BAUD_DIV | [15:0] | DIV | `0x1b1` | Reset 433 (bit period 434 cycles). |
| IRQ_EN | [4] | TX_OVF | `0x0` |  |
| IRQ_EN | [3] | RX_OVF | `0x0` |  |
| IRQ_EN | [2] | FRAME_ERR | `0x0` |  |
| IRQ_EN | [1] | TX | `0x0` |  |
| IRQ_EN | [0] | RX | `0x0` |  |
| IRQ_STATUS | [4] | TX_OVF | `0x0` | Sticky: DATA written with the TX FIFO full. |
| IRQ_STATUS | [3] | RX_OVF | `0x0` | Sticky: a byte arrived with the RX FIFO full (the byte is dropped). |
| IRQ_STATUS | [2] | FRAME_ERR | `0x0` | Sticky: a stop bit sampled 0 (the byte is dropped). |
| IRQ_STATUS | [1] | TX | `0x1` | Level: TX FIFO empty. |
| IRQ_STATUS | [0] | RX | `0x0` | Level: RX_LEVEL > CTRL.RX_THRESH. |

## GPIO

8-bit GPIO with a direction register and per-pin edge interrupts.

| Address | Register | Access | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x40001000` | GPIO_IN | RO | `0x00000000` | Pin levels after a 2-flop synchroniser. |
| `0x40001004` | GPIO_OUT | RW | `0x00000000` | Output values (driven only where DIR=1). |
| `0x40001008` | GPIO_DIR | RW | `0x00000000` | Direction, 1 = output. |
| `0x4000100c` | GPIO_RISE_EN | RW | `0x00000000` | Interrupt on a rising edge of IN. |
| `0x40001010` | GPIO_FALL_EN | RW | `0x00000000` | Interrupt on a falling edge of IN. |
| `0x40001014` | GPIO_IRQ_STATUS | W1C | `0x00000000` | Edge seen on an enabled pin; write 1 to clear. |

| Register | Bits | Field | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IN | [7:0] | IN | `0x0` | One bit per pin. |
| OUT | [7:0] | OUT | `0x0` | One bit per pin. |
| DIR | [7:0] | DIR | `0x0` | Reset: all inputs. |
| RISE_EN | [7:0] | EN | `0x0` | One bit per pin. |
| FALL_EN | [7:0] | EN | `0x0` | One bit per pin. |
| IRQ_STATUS | [7:0] | PEND | `0x0` | One bit per pin. |

## TIMER

CLINT-style machine timer and software interrupt (privileged spec §3.2.1 and §3.1.9). Drives mip.MTIP (mtime >= mtimecmp, unsigned 64-bit) and mip.MSIP directly, not through the IRQ controller. Compact offsets (not the SiFive CLINT layout).

| Address | Register | Access | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x40002000` | TIMER_MSIP | RW | `0x00000000` | Machine software interrupt pending (mip.MSIP). |
| `0x40002008` | TIMER_MTIMECMP_LO | RW | `0xffffffff` | mtimecmp[31:0]. |
| `0x4000200c` | TIMER_MTIMECMP_HI | RW | `0xffffffff` | mtimecmp[63:32]. |
| `0x40002010` | TIMER_MTIME_LO | RW | `0x00000000` | mtime[31:0]. |
| `0x40002014` | TIMER_MTIME_HI | RW | `0x00000000` | mtime[63:32]. |
| `0x40002018` | TIMER_PRESCALE | RW | `0x00000000` | mtime tick divider. |

| Register | Bits | Field | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MSIP | [0] | MSIP | `0x0` |  |
| MTIMECMP_LO | [31:0] | VAL | `0xffffffff` | Reset all ones, so MTIP=0 after reset. |
| MTIMECMP_HI | [31:0] | VAL | `0xffffffff` |  |
| MTIME_LO | [31:0] | VAL | `0x0` |  |
| MTIME_HI | [31:0] | VAL | `0x0` |  |
| PRESCALE | [15:0] | DIV | `0x0` | 0 = mtime counts every clock. |

## IRQC

Simple 8-source interrupt controller. mip.MEIP = |(PENDING & ENABLE). Sources are levels.

| Address | Register | Access | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x40003000` | IRQC_PENDING | RO | `0x00000000` | Current level of each source (0 UART, 1 GPIO, 2 PMU, 3-7 tied 0). |
| `0x40003004` | IRQC_ENABLE | RW | `0x00000000` | Source enables. |

| Register | Bits | Field | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PENDING | [7:0] | SRC | `0x0` | One bit per source. |
| ENABLE | [7:0] | EN | `0x0` | One bit per source. |

## SYSCTRL

Boot and wake reason, scratch, boot strap (AON, survives DEEP_SLEEP).

| Address | Register | Access | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x40004000` | SYSCTRL_ID | RO | `0x4c503332` | Chip identification. |
| `0x40004004` | SYSCTRL_RESET_CAUSE | W1C | `0x00000001` | Why the core last left reset. |
| `0x40004008` | SYSCTRL_WAKE_SRC | W1C | `0x00000000` | Which wake source(s) fired since last cleared (one bit per PMU wake_irq input). |
| `0x4000400c` | SYSCTRL_SCRATCH | RW | `0x00000000` | General-purpose AON storage; keeps its value across DEEP_SLEEP (not across cold reset). |
| `0x40004010` | SYSCTRL_BOOT | RO | `0x00000000` | Boot strap pin, sampled at cold reset. |
| `0x40004014` | SYSCTRL_UART_WAKE_EN | RW | `0x00000000` | Enables the AON UART-RX start-bit detector (wake_irq[1]). |

| Register | Bits | Field | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ID | [31:0] | ID | `0x4c503332` | ASCII "LP32". |
| RESET_CAUSE | [1] | WARM | `0x0` | Core domain powered up again by the PMU after DEEP_SLEEP (warm boot). |
| RESET_CAUSE | [0] | COLD | `0x1` | Power-on / external reset (rst_n pin). |
| WAKE_SRC | [2] | TIMER | `0x0` | wake_irq[2]: mtime >= mtimecmp. |
| WAKE_SRC | [1] | UART_RX | `0x0` | wake_irq[1]: UART RX start bit (AON detector). |
| WAKE_SRC | [0] | CORE_IRQ | `0x0` | wake_irq[0]: an enabled interrupt (mip & mie) while the core was clock-gated (IDLE). |
| SCRATCH | [31:0] | VAL | `0x0` |  |
| BOOT | [0] | SEL | `0x0` | 0 = boot ROM loads the program over UART; 1 = jump to IMEM (memory preloaded, simulation). |
| UART_WAKE_EN | [0] | EN | `0x0` |  |

## PMU

P2 power-management unit (soc-pmu-sequencer / multipower). Register map imported from its YAML (provisional copy pinned in vendor/VENDOR.md until P2 is merged).

Registers imported from `vendor/pmu/regmap.yaml`.

| `0x40005008` | PMU_MODE_REQ | RW | `0x00000000` | Requested system mode. |
| `0x4000500c` | PMU_MODE_STATUS | RO | `0x00000004` | Current system status. |

| `0x4000501c` | PMU_WAKE_TIMER_CMP | RW | `0xffffffff` | Wake-timer compare value. |
| `0x40005020` | PMU_WAKE_TIMER | RO | `0x00000000` | AON wake-timer count (PMU clock cycles since the timer was enabled). |

| `0x40005050` | PMU_DLY_RET | RW | `0x00000002` | Width of the ret_save / ret_restore pulse in cycles. |
| `0x40005054` | PMU_DLY_RST | RW | `0x00000002` | Cycles held after an rst_n change before the next step. |
| `0x40005060` | PMU_TMO_QCH | RW | `0x00000100` | Maximum cycles to wait for any Q-Channel response. |

| Register | Bits | Field | Reset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ID | [31:0] | ID | `0x504d5530` | ASCII "PMU0". |
| VERSION | [31:16] | MAJOR | `0x1` | Incremented on incompatible map changes. |
| VERSION | [15:0] | MINOR | `0x0` | Incremented on compatible additions. |
| MODE_REQ | [2:0] | MODE | `0x0` | Target mode. (mode encoding) |
| MODE_STATUS | [10] | MISMATCH | `0x0` | Not busy, but some domain is not at the target of MODE_REQ (a deny left it in place). |
| MODE_STATUS | [9] | FAULT | `0x0` | At least one domain is in FAULT. |

| MODE_STATUS | [2:0] | MODE | `0x4` | Last mode reached in full (every domain at its target). Reset: SHUTDOWN (all domains OFF). (mode encoding) |
| PD_STATE | [19] | PERI_BUSY | `0x0` | PD_PERI is in a sequence. |

| PD_STATE | [3] | CPU_BUSY | `0x0` | PD_CPU is in a sequence. |
| PD_STATE | [2:0] | CPU_STATE | `0x3` | PD_CPU stable state. (pd_state encoding) |
| WAKE_MODE | [2:0] | MODE | `0x0` | Wake target mode. (mode encoding) |
| WAKE_MASK | [7:0] | MASK | `0xff` | 1 = wake_irq[i] ignored. Reset: all masked. |

| WAKE_CTRL | [0] | TIMER_EN | `0x0` | Writing 1 clears WAKE_TIMER and starts it. Hardware clears this bit when the compare fires (one-shot). |
| DLY_TRICKLE | [15:0] | CYCLES | `0x8` | 0 is treated as 1. |
| DLY_MAIN | [15:0] | CYCLES | `0x4` | 0 is treated as 1. |
| DLY_CLK | [15:0] | CYCLES | `0x2` | 0 is treated as 1. |
| DLY_ISO | [15:0] | CYCLES | `0x2` | 0 is treated as 1. |
| DLY_RET | [15:0] | CYCLES | `0x2` | 0 is treated as 1. |
| DLY_RST | [15:0] | CYCLES | `0x2` | 0 is treated as 1. |
| TMO_QCH | [15:0] | CYCLES | `0x100` | Timeout leads to FAULT. 0 = 65536. |
| TMO_PSW | [15:0] | CYCLES | `0x100` | Timeout leads to FAULT. 0 = 65536. |
| IRQ_STATUS | [3] | WAKE | `0x0` | A wake event (unmasked wake_irq or timer compare) occurred. |
| IRQ_STATUS | [2] | FAULT | `0x0` | A wait step timed out (details in FAULT_INFO). Clearing it releases FAULT domains to OFF. |
| IRQ_STATUS | [1] | DENY | `0x0` | A domain denied a quiescence request (Q_DENIED); it stayed in place. |
| IRQ_STATUS | [0] | DONE | `0x0` | A transition finished with every domain at its target. |
| IRQ_EN | [3] | WAKE | `0x0` |  |
| IRQ_EN | [2] | FAULT | `0x1` |  |
| IRQ_EN | [1] | DENY | `0x0` |  |
| IRQ_EN | [0] | DONE | `0x0` |  |
| FAULT_INFO | [31] | VALID | `0x0` | FAULT_INFO holds a fault. |
| FAULT_INFO | [6:4] | STEP | `0x0` | The wait step that timed out. (fault_step encoding) |
| FAULT_INFO | [1:0] | DOMAIN | `0x0` | Domain index (0 CPU |

**mode**: RUN = 0, IDLE = 1, SLEEP = 2, DEEP_SLEEP = 3, SHUTDOWN = 4

**pd_state**: ON = 0, CLK_GATED = 1, RET = 2, OFF = 3, FAULT = 7

**fault_step**: QACCEPT_DOWN = 1, QDENY_RELEASE = 2, PSW_MAIN_OFF = 3, PSW_TRICKLE_OFF = 4, PSW_TRICKLE_ON = 5, PSW_MAIN_ON = 6, QACCEPT_UP = 7
